newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila, Moslem rebels fail to agree on pullback.
newsitem.headline: Manila, Moslem rebels fail to agree on pullback.

text.p: Government and Moslem rebel negotiators failed to reach agreement on Thursday on a proposed pullback of their forces in an embattled town in the southern Philippines.

"They agreed on nothing," a member of Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) panel told reporters after the meeting, which was called to defuse tension around nearby Buldon town where more than 40 people have died in clashes since January.
The Cotabato talks followed fresh fighting between rebels and the military in a neighbouring province in which more than 30 people have been killed in the past week.
The two sides are to meet again on May 13-14, officials said at the end of two-day talks in the southern Philippine city.

The army has deployed about 1,500 troops around Buldon separated by only about 400 metres from hundreds of MILF guerrillas also entrenched in foothill villages around the town, residents of the town said.
This week's talks were called to discuss a proposal for the two forces to pull four km (2.5 miles) back from their positions.
The meeting was also meant to negotiate an interim ceasefire ahead of formal negotiations on ending the MILF-led rebellion.

The MILF, a breakaway rebel faction fighting for an Islamic state, is not a party to the peace agreement signed by Manila in September last year with the mainstream Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF).
The September deal ended a 24-year MNLF-led revolt for autonomy which claimed about 125,000 lives.
